signals.evidence: Air raid sirens activated in Upper Galilee border towns near Lebanon with immediate shelter-in-place directives issued in preparation for potential rocket attack
Firefighters handled suspicious package at airport with precautionary evacuation; military intercepted rocket launched from Iran toward northern territory
News anchor reiterates safety advisories and repeated calls for civilian compliance with Home Front directives
Senior Sergeant Gai Ludari killed by friendly fire during Hezbollah terrorist detention operation in village of Shiba in Lebanon
Police clashes with anti-war demonstrators near Habima Theatre; at least 17 demonstrators detained; one injured and lost consciousness when air raid alarm sounded
Supreme Court ruled to expand permitted demonstration participation from 150 to 600 people, contradicting Home Front Command safety restrictions
Schools expected to resume teaching April 12 in reduced format after Passover closure; Ben-Gurion Airport flight restrictions being eased
Home Front Command Colonel Aviberma: 'Passover camps are open and permitted. Special education for children with special needs is also allowed' with requirement to reach shelter within 60 seconds
Home Front Command Colonel: 'Some municipalities have not accepted this, some have complied' regarding shelter proximity requirements for special needs schools
Home Front Command official: '80% of injuries during this war occurred at home as a result of careless actions heading to shelters'
Home Front Command official emphasizes careful, methodical responses to alerts: stopping vehicles safely on roadsides, using emergency signals, entering shelters cautiously
Home Front Command Colonel: 'We all bow to court decisions even if we don't like them. Home Front Command tries to allow routine life to continue on one hand while preserving life on the other'
Home Front Command official advises civilians to use Home Front Command mobile application with location services enabled to receive threat alerts during outdoor activities

Northern education director: 'Much less damage in the north today... The citizens are standing at the front, they are the spearhead, they mark the way for us, and we must appreciate the people of the north very much'
Northern education director: civilians have adapted to brief 15-second warning periods; much incoming fire directed at Israeli military forces within Lebanon rather than civilian targets

Official addresses immigrant population: 'Every one of us is doing something for the success of the war. If you are parents to children, take care of them, engage them, create connection with them... the most important thing is to take care of children—this is part of the war effort'
Supreme Court Chief Justice Yitzhak Amit: 'if we prohibit demonstrations, then this will no longer be a democratic state'
Football matches resuming without spectators during wartime
Senior sergeant killed in friendly fire during counter-terrorism operation in southern Lebanon; Iran launched missile attacks on Israel and Kuwait with air defense interceptions
Education correspondent: 'First, regarding children returning—all of classes 1, 2, and probably 3, and of course also secure classes 4-1 and 4-2' contingent on Home Front Command security approval
Education correspondent: 'Everything is very differential; some cities have no shelter at all, some authorities have nowhere even to hold studies'

Correspondent: 'Some cities have no shelter at all, so we have no classes because we have no protected space. For younger age groups this will be somewhat more complicated because most facilities are less protected or lack shelter entirely'
Education correspondent: 'We still continue the traffic light system; there are red, orange, yellow—it's constantly changing' with different municipalities maintaining different preparedness levels

Education official: 'Many educational institutions are still serving as shelters. Not every neighborhood has a shelter—some have none at all. There are no clear answers. We don't know what happens with transportation'
Education official: 'The final decision will only be made after consultations before the second holiday, seemingly on Tuesday and the days preceding the return to school'

Correspondent: 'The intention is to return preschoolers, first, second, and possibly third graders, and exam-year students after Passover. But in what form, how—that's still unclear. Each municipality will ultimately make decisions based on their own reasoning'
Correspondent: 'Transportation for regular students remains uncertain; only students with special needs will have reliable shuttle access'

Education official: 'No one clearly understands who will take responsibility. There's no way to safely operate the shuttles. The situation where children must shelter during an alert while on a shuttle—that's also very complicated'
Ministry of Transport raised permitted passenger load on outbound flights from 50 to 80 persons per departure; only one outbound and one inbound flight per hour permitted
In ordinary Passover week, 1.5 million Israelis travel; current operations severely restricted with only one outbound and one inbound flight per hour
Of 80 available seats per flight, only 20 designated for humanitarian cases; remaining 60 allocated by ticket purchase date, creating queue-based allocation for stranded travelers
Israeli airlines operating at drastically reduced capacity with near-empty flights generating minimal revenue; foreign airlines entirely barred from operating to Israel under government restrictions
Regulatory adjustment does not trigger meaningful resumption of commercial operations; aviation sector remains in critical operational paralysis
Passenger metrics remain drastically below normal aircraft seating capacity; system will take many weeks or months to process backlog of stranded travelers
